title: The ox forgotten
hook: picture seven: home, the ox forgotten, the herder at rest (Ox-Herding 7)
tomorrow: what's left in the picture when even the herder goes?

segments.voice: That was a week of pictures: a search, tracks, a glimpse, a pull, a rope, and a flute. Yesterday's line: riding home, the long work turned into music. Today he arrives.

The first week on a new bike, every pedal takes thought. A year later you ride to the shop and can't remember the ride. Kuoan's seventh picture is that later day. The herder is home, sitting outside his hut in the sun. He isn't searching, or holding, or riding. He's just sitting. And the ox is nowhere. Not lost this time. Forgotten, because there's nothing left to manage.
screen: `THE RIDE YOU DON'T REMEMBER.` → `HOME, IN THE SUN.` → `THE OX IS NOWHERE.`

segments.voice: The preface explains: there are not two things. The ox was only a stand-in, like a trap set for a hare, or a net for a fish. That echoes Zhuangzi, the Taoist sage, who said that once you have the fish, you can forget the trap. The verse: the ox is gone, the man sits at peace; the red sun is high, and he's still dozing; whip and rope lie idle under the thatched roof. The Buddha had his own image for this, in the parable of the raft: you build it to cross the river, and you don't carry it on your head once you're across. Zen's teaching here: the method serves the way, and it can be set down. At rest isn't laziness. It's the practice finally sitting still inside you. The preface has an image for it: like gold drawn out of ore, like the moon coming out from behind clouds. Nothing new was made; something was uncovered. Six pictures brought him here. Searching, alone in the grass. The footprints, found in the teachings. A glimpse, through a bird's song. It pulls, toward the sweet grass. The rope, held close every day. Riding home, with a flute.
screen: `NOT TWO THINGS.` · `FORGET THE TRAP, KEEP THE FISH.` · `THE RAFT STAYS ON THE SHORE.` · `ROPE IDLE UNDER THE ROOF.` · then, large: `AT REST.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes for the two minutes, and don't do anything with the breath: no counting, no rope, no fixing. Let the body sit the way the herder sits in the sun. If you catch yourself checking whether you're resting correctly, that's the ox; let it go too.
The ox forgotten: Kuoan's seventh picture. The herder at home, the method set down, nothing left to manage.
Pocket this: at rest, whip and rope idle under the roof. Seven pictures in, and a week behind you.

howItsDone: Zen students read the seventh picture as the method set down once it has done its work; Buddhists know the Buddha's parable of the raft. People on this path let a rest day be rest.

fork.setup: a man crosses a river on a raft he built, then hoists it onto his head to carry everywhere. what does the Buddha's parable say?
options: leave it on the shore: the raft was for crossing, not for carrying.
carry it always, out of gratitude for the crossing it gave him.
keep it close in case another river shows up someday.
fork.reveal: in the parable of the raft, the Buddha says the wise man leaves it at the shore. Kuoan's herder does the same with the ox: the method can be set down.

original.note: Chinese: the ox forgotten, the man remains, the title of Kuoan's seventh picture.

trapdoor: what you thought: forgetting the ox means losing it again.
what it means: there were never two; the method can be set down, like a trap once the hare is caught.
what a scholar hears: the preface borrows Zhuangzi's trap and net; the Buddha's raft in the Majjhima Nikaya makes the same move.

chat.says: lazy sunday, did nothing. felt guilty, like now that i lead i should be practicing harder.
options: picture seven: the rope lies idle at home. resting isn't slacking; it's the next picture.
the guilt is your rope: keep it tight, because leaders shouldn't take a day off.
rest comes only at the very last picture; seven is still all about hard effort.
chat.meaning: In Kuoan's seventh picture the herder sits at home, the ox forgotten, whip and rope idle. Like Zhuangzi's trap, the method can be set down.

tie.story: Home at last, Kuoan's herder forgot the ox and sat at rest, whip and rope idle under his roof.
tie.friend: Zoe's lazy Sunday is picture seven, not slacking; the method can rest too.
